Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 63, verses 1–3:

﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah."﴾ They would say with their tongues what was not in their hearts, so Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿And Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.﴾ That is, they lied in their claim to bear witness to the Messenger-hood. As for His saying, ﴿And Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger,﴾ it is not part of the speech of the hypocrites; rather, it is from the speech of Allah, the Exalted. Had He not mentioned it, it would have given the impression that His saying, "Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars," is an invalidation of the Messenger-hood. So He placed it between the report about the hypocrites and their refutation, in order to remove this misconception and to affirm the Messenger-hood. Based on this, it is appropriate to pause at His saying, "indeed the Messenger of Allah." ﴿A shield﴾ is mentioned in al-Mujadila [16]: ﴿That is because they believed and then disbelieved.﴾ The reference is to the evil of their deeds, their disgrace and their reproach. As for His saying, "they believed and then disbelieved," it may have two meanings: one is that it refers to those among them who had a sound belief and then became hypocrites afterwards; the other is that it means they professed belief outwardly, like His saying: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾ [al-Baqarah 14].

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 63, verse 4:

﴿And when you see them, their bodies please you﴾ meaning: they are fine in appearance. ﴿And if they speak, you listen to their speech﴾ meaning: they are eloquent in speech. The pronoun in His saying ﴿when you see them, [their bodies] please you﴾ and in His saying ﴿you listen to their speech﴾ refers to the Prophet ﷺ and to every addressee. ﴿As if they were propped-up pieces of wood﴾: He likened them to wood in their lack of understanding, so they had an outward appearance without any inner substance. Al-Zamakhshari said: He likened them to pieces of wood propped against a wall, because wood in that condition has no benefit, unlike wood that is in a roof or planted in a wall, for that has benefit. So the comparison, on this view, is in the lack of benefit. It was also said: they used to lean back in the gathering of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so He likened their leaning to propped-up pieces of wood against a wall. ﴿They think every shout is against them﴾ is an expression of the intensity of their fear of the Muslims, for when they heard a shout they thought that the Prophet ﷺ was ordering their killing. ﴿May Allah destroy them﴾: the curse upon them includes a condemnation of them and a denunciation of their condition. ﴿How are they turned away?﴾ meaning: how are they diverted from faith when it is so manifest?

When it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you," they turn their heads aside. ﴿لَوَّوْاْ رُءُوسَهُمْ﴾ means they tilt them away, in aversion and arrogance.

The story behind this verse and what follows is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out on the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq. The people reached a water source over which they crowded. Among those who crowded for it were Jahjah ibn Sa'id, a hired man of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Sinan al-Juhani, an ally of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the leader of the hypocrites. Jahjah struck Sinan, so Sinan became angry and called out to the Ansar, and Jahjah called out to the Muhajirun. Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: "By Allah, our case and theirs (meaning the Muhajirun) is nothing but what the first one said: 'Fatten your dog and it will devour you.'" Then he said: "If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it." By "the mightier" he meant himself and his followers, and by "the meaner" he meant the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and those with him. Then he said to his people: "These Muhajirun stay in Medina only because of your support and your spending on them. If you cut that off from them, they would flee from your city."

Zayd ibn Arqam heard this and informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of it, and the report reached Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. He swore that he had said nothing of that kind, and he denied Zayd. Thereupon the surah was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Zayd and said: "Allah has verified you, O Zayd." Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul was disgraced, and people despised him. It was said to him: "Go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) so that he may ask forgiveness for you," but he turned his head away in refusal of this suggestion and said: "You ordered me to embrace Islam and I embraced it; you ordered me to pay the zakat on my wealth and I did it. Nothing remains for you but to order me to prostrate to Muhammad." Abdullah ibn Ubayy died shortly after that.

The sayings that Abdullah ibn Ubayy uttered were attributed to the plural pronoun, because he had followers among the hypocrites who agreed with him in them.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 63, verse 6:

﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾ It is narrated that when the verse ﴿Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 80] was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will surely add to the seventy." When Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions did what they did, Allah made this surah more severe toward them and informed that He would not forgive them in any way. But this requires consideration, because this surah was revealed at the battle of Banu al-Mustaliq, a period before the other verse.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 63, verse 9:

﴿Let not your wealth or your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah﴾. That is: do not let them preoccupy you. The remembrance of Allah here is general, covering prayer, supplication, and worship in all its forms. It has been said that it refers specifically to the prescribed prayer (al-salat al-maktubah), but the general meaning is more preferable.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 63, verse 10:

﴿And spend of what We have provided you﴾. This is general in meaning, covering zakat (obligatory almsgiving), voluntary charity (ṣadaqat al-taṭawwuʿ), spending in jihad (striving in the way of God), and other things. It was also said that it means only the obligatory zakat, but the general meaning is more appropriate. ﴿And I would be among the righteous﴾. With the jussive (bi-l-jazm), it is coordinated (ʿaṭf) on the place of the response to the condition (jawāb al-sharṭ). Abu ʿAmr read فأكونَ with the accusative (bi-l-naṣb), coordinated on فأصدقَ.
